settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: No code in the read source proves a remotely reachable, unauthenticated REST/UI path to compileYangFiles; callers were not read.
A canonical-path validation could exist in the caller or in the unread service registration; not observed in the read span.
candidates.description: extractZipArchive iterates ZIP entries and builds the destination as new File(dir, entry.getName()) with no canonical-containment check. compilesYangFiles() (line 73-74) takes an attacker-influenced InputStream; when the stream's first bytes are "PK" (isZipArchive, lines 102/208-209), extraction runs. A zip entry name such as "../../<target>" (or an absolute name) causes guava Files.createParentDirs + Files.write to create directories and write the file outside the intended temp root, giving arbitrary file write with the process's privileges. The XML/YANG compilation and JAR assembly steps make the resulting content potentially executable code loaded by the platform. Reachability of compileYangFiles from a remote, unauthenticated caller was not verifiable in the read source.
missing_evidence: The REST/UI resource (e.g. YangWebResource) that invokes compileYangFiles, and its authentication/authorization gating.
YangLiveCompilerService interface contract and any input validation performed before extraction.
Whether the deployment runs with elevated privileges for the ONOS process.
preconditions: The attacker can supply the yangSources stream to compileYangFiles (modelId + InputStream) with bytes beginning with "PK".
The compressed archive contains an entry whose name uses path traversal ("..") or an absolute path.
The process has write permission to the target location outside the temp root.
candidates.title: Zip Slip arbitrary file write in YangLiveCompilerManager ZIP extraction

counter_evidence: The String[] API passes arguments without a shell, so classic command-injection via spaces/"&" is not demonstrated.
modelId may be constrained by the service caller or validated by the script; script contents were not read.
candidates.description: runJavaCompiler and runJarAssembly execute Runtime.getRuntime().exec(new String[]{"bash", script.getAbsolutePath(), <abs path>, <abs path>, modelId}), forwarding the caller-supplied modelId as a positional argument to a shell script written from a classpath resource (writeResource, lines 201-205). The String[] form blocks shell metacharacter splitting, but the script's handling of modelId (option parsing with a leading "-", quoting, use in further commands) was not readable, so argument/option injection or command execution cannot be confirmed or excluded. Recorded as a candidate whose severity depends on unread script contents.
missing_evidence: Contents of the onos-yang-javac and onos-yang-jar resource scripts (how modelId is consumed).
The YangLiveCompilerService caller and any validation of modelId.
Reachability of the service from remote untrusted input.
preconditions: A caller can pass an attacker-controlled modelId into compileYangFiles.
The generated onos-yang-javac / onos-yang-jar scripts interpret modelId in a way influenced by its content (e.g., leading dashes or unquoted expansion).
candidates.title: Untrusted modelId passed as argument to generated bash script (argument injection risk) in YangLiveCompilerManager

counter_evidence: Jersey normally decodes and may reject some path segments, and the classloader resource lookup may not allow filesystem traversal; not verified.
No validation or lack of validation in getStream was observed because lines 121-282 were not read.
candidates.description: UiExtension.resource(viewId, path) concatenates user-influenced values into a classloader resource name: getStream("app/view/" + viewId + "/" + path). MainViewResource.getViewResource maps REST path parameters {view} and {resource} straight into extension.resource(viewId, resource). If getStream does not normalize/validate the resulting resource name, a crafted resource value could traverse out of the view directory when resolving the resource. The read span ends at line 120, so getStream and any validation were not examined; this is recorded strictly as an unconfirmed candidate.
missing_evidence: Implementation of getStream and any normalization/allow-list it performs.
Whether the REST endpoints enforce authentication/authorization before reaching this method.
preconditions: An unauthenticated or low-privilege client can call GET /{view}/{resource} on the REST endpoint.
getStream resolves the concatenated resource name without rejecting ".." segments or absolute paths (unverified).
candidates.title: User-controlled view/resource path built into extension resource name in UiExtension.resource (path traversal depends on unread getStream)
